title: Number Quest Unit 6 · The Drafting Keep (Pro)

items.q: A box is 1 1/2 m long, 2 m wide and 1 m high. How many cubes with edges of 1/2 m fill it?
misconceptions: found the volume in cubic meters and stopped
divided the volume by 1/2 only once
correct
added the cubes along each edge instead of multiplying
items.why: Count the cubes along each edge: 3 along 1 1/2 m, 4 along 2 m and 2 along 1 m. Then 3 × 4 × 2 = 24. Check: the volume is 3 m³ and each cube is 1/8 m³.

items.q: A box is 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. Unfold it into its net. What is its surface area?
misconceptions: counted only three of the six faces
correct
found the volume instead of the area of the faces
added the three edge lengths
items.why: The net has three pairs of faces: 4 × 3 = 12, 4 × 2 = 8 and 3 × 2 = 6. Each pair counts twice: 2 × (12 + 8 + 6) = 52 cm².

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 4 m and 10 m. The distance between them is 6 m. What is its area?
misconceptions: multiplied the sum of the parallel sides by the height without halving
multiplied the longer side by the height
used only the shorter side times the height
correct
items.why: Cut it into a rectangle and triangles, or use the mean of the parallel sides: (4 + 10) ÷ 2 = 7, and 7 × 6 = 42 m².

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One of the four angles is 48°. What is the angle next to it?
misconceptions: took the angle across from it, which is equal
subtracted from 90° instead of 180°
correct
subtracted from 360° instead of 180°
items.why: Angles next to each other on a straight line add to 180°. So the angle next to 48° is 180° − 48° = 132°. The angle across from 48° is also 48°.

items.q: Point P (3, −2) is reflected over the y-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
misconceptions: reflected it over the x-axis instead
correct
changed both signs, which is a half turn
swapped the two coordinates
items.why: A flip over the y-axis changes the side, not the height: (x, y) becomes (−x, y). So (3, −2) becomes (−3, −2).

items.q: A triangle with sides of 3, 4 and 5 units is turned 90° about the origin. How long are its sides after the turn?
choices: It depends on how far it is from the origin
misconceptions: correct
thought a quarter turn doubles each side
squared each side length
thought a turn stretches a shape far from the origin
items.why: A turn moves every point but keeps every length and every angle. The image is congruent to the triangle: its sides are still 3, 4 and 5 units.

items.q: A ladder 10 m long leans on a wall. Its foot is 6 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
misconceptions: subtracted the lengths instead of their squares
added the two lengths
added the squares instead of subtracting them
correct
items.why: The ladder is the long side: 6² + h² = 10². So h² = 100 − 36 = 64, and h = √64 = 8 m.

items.q: What is the distance between the points (−1, 2) and (5, 10)?
misconceptions: added the distance across and the distance up
correct
stopped before taking the square root
took the difference of the distance across and up

items.q: A room is 4 m long, 3 m wide and 12 m tall. How long is the longest pole from a floor corner to the far top corner?
misconceptions: found only the diagonal of the floor
added the three edges
correct
used only the length and the height
items.why: The floor's diagonal: 4² + 3² = 25, so 5 m. Then 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169, and √169 = 13 m.
